# The host protocol

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_host_protocol (python3 -m provenstream.openrpc --markdown) from the host's registry
(host/provenstream/host.py), the core engine's description and the answer table (host/provenstream/protocol.py). Do
not edit: scripts/check.sh regenerates it and fails when this file differs. -->

How callers talk to a Provenstream host: protocol 2, host version 0.1.0. The engine behind the host has
its own line protocol, [PROTOCOL.md](PROTOCOL.md); this is the outer one, the same whatever carries the bytes. A host
answers `rpc.discover` with this description as an OpenRPC 1.3.2 document (methods, params, results, errors), for
tools and generated clients.

## Messages

JSON-RPC 2.0. One request object per message: `{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": ID, "method": NAME, "params": {...}}`,
with `id` a string, an integer or null and `params` an object (absent is `{}`). JSON is read strictly: a repeated
key, `NaN` or a lone surrogate is `parse_error`. Batches and notifications (no `id`) are `invalid_request` in protocol
2, so every request gets exactly one answer. A message over 1048576 bytes (1 MiB) is `invalid_request`. Every error's `data`
holds `"code"`, the name of its row in the answer table below.

| carrier | how | caller |
|---|---|---|
| in process | `Host.open(db, engines).handle(message, auth)`, or `host.command(name, auth=..., **params)` / `host.query(...)` | `Token(t)` or `Operator(principal)` |
| stdio | `provenstream serve --stdio`: one request per line on stdin, one answer per line on stdout, in order | one per session, fixed at launch: `--as PRINCIPAL` or `--token-file FILE` |
| HTTP | `provenstream serve`: `POST /rpc` (always HTTP 200; the outcome is in the body), `GET /healthz` | `Authorization: Bearer TOKEN` |

The answer to a message is the same bytes on every carrier for the same caller. The cases of
[conformance/](conformance/README.md) check a host against this document (`provenstream conform`, on any carrier or
against a host at a URL); a host that passes them is Provenstream-compatible for protocol 2.

## Callers

A token names its caller; no token, or one the host does not know, is `unauthorized`. `Operator(principal)` exists
in process only: whoever holds the database is already the host, and acts as any principal the store knows (as
`--as` does on the command line). `Operator(None)` is the operator as no principal: it may call what needs none.

A principal is an id and its tokens: no kind, no role, no account. Every proof command carries the caller's
`actor_id`: the token's principal (or the operator's), filled in when the caller leaves it out, and refused
`actor_id_must_match_the_token` when it names another.

**Reads.** Reading is unrestricted: any authenticated principal reads any stream (no proof says who reads). A read of a
stream with no rows is refused `stream_must_exist`.

**Paging.** `stream.events` and `stream.rows` answer at most `limit` rows (default and most 1000) from seq `from`
(default 0), and `next`: the `from` of the next page, or null at the end.

**Revisions.** A revision is a commit and a package path, so one commit serves all its proofs side by side. Its URL:
`<repo>/commit/<commit>` (or `<repo>#<commit>`, `<repo>@<commit>`) names the repository's root package,
`<repo>/tree/<commit>/<package>` another (`<package>`: `/`-separated segments of `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, none `.` or `..`).
`revision.describe` and `revisions.list` name a revision by its key: `<commit>`, or `<commit>/<package>`.

## Answers

| `data.code` | JSON-RPC | CLI exit | when | `data` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ok` | result | 0 | done | the result |
| `parse_error` | -32700 | 5 | not strict JSON (a repeated key, NaN, a lone surrogate) | detail |
| `invalid_request` | -32600 | 5 | not one JSON-RPC 2.0 request: also a batch, a notification, a message over 1048576 bytes | detail |
| `method_not_found` | -32601 | 5 | neither in the host's registry nor described by the stream's revision | detail, for a proof command: the revision |
| `invalid_params` | -32602 | 5 | params malformed for the method's schema (the engine's malformed lands here) | detail |
| `unauthorized` | -32001 | 3 | no token, or one the host does not know; or a method that acts as a principal asked without one | detail, sometimes |
| `refused` | -32002 | 4 | a proof rule or a host check said no; nothing stored | reason: the rule broken |
| `unavailable` | -32003 | 6 | nothing stored; retry with the same idempotency key | retry: true, incident (the detail is logged under it, never sent) |

Every refusal's `data.reason` names the rule broken. The host's own: `stream_must_exist` (a command or a read naming a
stream with no rows), `revision_must_be_installed` (a `stream.open` or `revision.describe` naming a revision with no
engine here), `repository_must_match_the_engine` (a `stream.open` whose URL names another repository than its engine
was built from), `engine_must_implement_the_interface` (its engine does not implement the stream interface),
`actor_id_must_match_the_token`, `idempotency_key_must_match_its_request` (a key reused for another request), and for
`principal.create` `only_the_operator_can_reissue_a_principal` and `principal_must_have_no_token`. Any other reason is
the proof's rule (`ref_must_name_an_earlier_event`, the layer mechanism's, among them). A `stream.open` whose
`proof_revision_url` is a string but no revision URL is refused with the core's own rule,
`revision_url_must_name_a_commit`, the host reading the URL exactly as the core does (it names no engine to ask); a
missing or non-string URL is `invalid_params`. `unavailable` never carries the
failure's text: it is logged under the incident id.

## Host methods

Queries change nothing and are safe to retry; host commands change the host's state, never a stream.

### `principal.create`

A host command: a new principal and its first token (with `principal_id`, the operator only: a first token for an id this store holds no token for). Caller: any authenticated caller, or the operator as no principal.

| param | | type | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `principal_id` | optional | UUID |  |

Result: {principal_id, token}.

### `revision.describe`

A query: the description of a revision this host serves. Caller: any authenticated caller, or the operator as no principal.

| param | | type | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `revision` | required | string | a revision: a full commit, and /<package> for a package other than the root |

Result: {revision, repo, package, protocol, schema}.

### `revisions.list`

A query: the revisions this host serves (a commit and a package each), and whether each engine runs now. Caller: any authenticated caller, or the operator as no principal.

No params.

Result: {revisions}.

### `rpc.discover`

A query: this host's OpenRPC document: every method, and every served revision's commands. Caller: any authenticated caller, or the operator as no principal.

No params.

Result: an OpenRPC 1.3 document.

### `stream.describe`

A query: the description of the stream's revision (its commands). Caller: any authenticated caller, or the operator as no principal.

| param | | type | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stream_id` | required | UUID |  |

Result: {revision, repo, package, protocol, schema}.

### `stream.events`

A query: a page of the stream's events, each with its seq and the chain head after it. Caller: any authenticated caller, or the operator as no principal.

| param | | type | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stream_id` | required | UUID |  |
| `from` | optional | integer (>= 0) |  |
| `limit` | optional | integer (>= 1, <= 1000) |  |

Result: {stream_id, events, next}.

### `stream.get`

A query: the stream as its revision's engine reads it. Caller: any authenticated caller, or the operator as no principal.

| param | | type | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stream_id` | required | UUID |  |

Result: {stream_id, opener_id, proof_revision_url, closed}.

### `stream.head`

A query: the stream's length and current chain head. Caller: any authenticated caller, or the operator as no principal.

| param | | type | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stream_id` | required | UUID |  |

Result: {stream_id, length, chain}.

### `stream.rows`

A query: a page of the stream's stored rows as stored, with meta salts and chain heads. Caller: any authenticated caller, or the operator as no principal.

| param | | type | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stream_id` | required | UUID |  |
| `from` | optional | integer (>= 0) |  |
| `limit` | optional | integer (>= 1, <= 1000) |  |

Result: {stream_id, rows, next}.

### `token.rotate`

A host command: a new token for the caller, the old one revoked. Caller: a principal (a token's, or the operator acting as one).

No params.

Result: {token}.

### `usage.get`

A query: usage counters: one stream's, or per revision. Caller: any authenticated caller, or the operator as no principal.

| param | | type | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scope` | optional | `stream` or `revision` |  |
| `key` | optional | string | a string: the stream or revision |

Result: {usage, notes}.

### `whoami`

A query: the caller's principal. Caller: a principal (a token's, or the operator acting as one).

No params.

Result: {principal_id}.

## Proof commands

Any other dotted name is a proof command: the stream's revision decides whether it exists (`method_not_found`, naming
the revision, if not) and whether to accept it. An accepted command appends exactly one event and answers `{seq,
event, chain}`; `chain` is the receipt, the stream's head after this row. A refused one stores nothing. Every proof
command takes an optional `idempotency_key`: a retry by the same caller with the same key answers the first answer,
and an optional `actor_id` (see Callers). Minted fields are fresh ids the host mints, in the event. The commands below
are the core's, which every revision has; a layer adds its own, listed by `rpc.discover`, by `stream.describe` and by
`provenstream -h --proof`.

### `stream.close`

Who may send it: the stream's opener.

| param | | type | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stream_id` | required | UUID |  |
| `meta` | optional | string or null | optional opaque text: at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes, no control character (committed to by the chain, erasable) |
| `actor_id` | optional | UUID |  |
| `idempotency_key` | optional | string (1 to 200 chars) |  |

Event `stream.closed`: {event, stream_id, actor_id, meta}. Minted: none.

Rules, in order: stream_must_exist, stream_must_be_open, only_opener_can_close.

### `stream.open`

Who may send it: anyone signed in; the caller becomes the stream's opener.

| param | | type | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `proof_revision_url` | required | string | text, its form checked by the engine |
| `meta` | optional | string or null | optional opaque text: at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes, no control character (committed to by the chain, erasable) |
| `actor_id` | optional | UUID |  |
| `idempotency_key` | optional | string (1 to 200 chars) |  |

Event `stream.opened`: {event, stream_id, actor_id, meta, proof_revision_url}. Minted: `stream_id`.

Rules, in order: stream_id_must_be_new, revision_url_must_name_a_commit.

## Versions

This is protocol 2 (`x-provenstream-protocol`). Within protocol 2 changes are additive only: new
methods, new optional params, new result keys, new refusal reasons. A caller ignores result keys it does not know. A
change to anything else (a code, a message, a param's meaning) is a new protocol. An engine's `describe` says its own
protocol (`"protocol": 2`); a host serves engines of protocol 2 only, listed by `rpc.discover`.
